text:
m1 - REACHABILITY, first instalment. TWO SITES SETTLED, and one of them is NOT what polarity predicted - which is the point of doing this rather than stopping at the partition.

SITE 1: sinkhorn.scala:44. REACHABLE, PROVEN BY EXECUTION, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT NaN.

SinkhornConfig is a PUBLIC CASE CLASS with no validation (sinkhorn.scala:5-11), so SinkhornConfig(epsilon = Double.NaN) is one keystroke from any caller. I ran it:

  NaN epsilon -> validator ACCEPTS -> plan = 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, converged=false, 200 iterations
  good config -> plan = 0.2543, 0.1025, 0.0413, 0.0166

So the validator fails open exactly as polarity predicted, and the caller gets a SILENTLY DEGENERATE ALL-ZERO TRANSPORT PLAN instead of Left(InvalidConfig), after burning the full iteration budget. NO NaN IS PUBLISHED. I expected NaN and did not get it, and I would have reported NaN if I had stopped at the polarity reading.

MITIGATION THAT MATTERS: converged=false IS returned. A caller who checks it can detect this. So the defect is "a validator that does not validate, and wastes 200 iterations", not "publishes a poisoned number". Real, and a grade less severe than the partition implied. Same for NaN rhoRows.

SITE 2: signature.scala:93 and :111, MassRatio - MINE. CONDITIONALLY REACHABLE, and NOT independently.

  MassRatio.of REFUSES NaN in both the numerator and the conditioning - I verified both return Left.
  So the checked door is sound; only `unsafe` is exposed, and it is private[align].
  A NaN can only reach it through a NaN row mass. AlignmentRow is `final class ... private[align]`,
  NOT a case class - already sealed by the earlier sweep - and its public door AlignmentRow.of
  REJECTS NaN (isWellFormed at matrix.scala:220).

  So NaN cannot enter from outside align. Inside align, the aligners build rows directly from
  emissions, and an emission is NaN only if a cost is NaN, which needs an upstream Estimate.observed(NaN).

THAT IS EXACTLY bd-01M174GMXJQ2YAZEMTANWN98Y4. So MassRatio's guard is the SECOND link in a chain whose first link is already filed as P1. Fixing finiteness at the source closes it; my guard is defence in depth, not the primary hole. I would still fix mine - a carrier whose purpose is refusing unsupported numbers should not admit NaN - but it should be ranked as hardening, not as a live defect, and it should NOT be done instead of the source fix.

WHAT REMAINS: nine fail-open sites unexamined - window.scala:122, population.scala:177 and :266, matrix.scala:175 and :217, density.scala:154, hsmm.scala:794, Smatch.scala:28, assess.scala:112. I have not started them and I am not going to guess. window.scala:122 is the one I would do next; it is the second instance of the exact recorded defect and its inputs come from feature samples rather than validated masses, so its upstream story is entirely different from align's.

The chief said a null result is a full result. Noted, and site 2 is most of the way to one.
